name: Lima
tagline: Coastal walks and a food-first arrival
summary: Use Lima for a gentle landing, coastal neighbourhoods and Peru’s archaeological context. Give its food and museums two real days before flying inland.
seasonNote: Coastal summer is sunnier; winter often has cool grey skies but remains good for museums and food.
arrival: LIM is outside the main visitor districts; use an authorized transfer and allow generous traffic time.
gettingAround: Group visits by Miraflores/Barranco, central Lima and Pueblo Libre; cross-city journeys can be slow.
cashTip: Cards are common in established restaurants; small soles notes help for markets and taxis.
foodTip: Ceviche is a classic lunch; also try causa, lomo saltado and picarones.
buyTip: Buy packaged coffee, chocolate, textiles or contemporary craft; confirm food import rules.
baseArea: Miraflores for convenience; Barranco for galleries and atmosphere.

items.name: Museo Larco
items.summary: A strong introduction to pre-Columbian Peru in an elegant museum setting.
items.expect: Ceramics, metalwork and gardens; allow time before continuing to another district.
items.tip: Useful early in a Peru trip so later archaeological visits have context.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult; check the current official price.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Ceramics and metalwork give a visual introduction to pre-Columbian Peru.
The museum setting and gardens make the context easier to absorb before a larger archaeology trip.
visitFlow: Start with the introductory galleries.
Look closely at selected ceramic and metal objects, then pause in the gardens.
items.tradeoffs: Ceramics, metalwork and gardens; allow time before continuing to another district.

items.name: Miraflores Malecón
items.summary: Clifftop paths connect ocean views, parks and cafés.
items.expect: Mostly easy walking with wind and changing coastal visibility.
items.tip: Walk between Parque del Amor and Larcomar; use sun protection even with cloud.

review.note: Miraflores Boardwalk listing, matching this coastal walking stop; not the broader Miraflores district. Review count is not footfall.

whyVisit: Clifftop paths link several parks with continuous Pacific views.
It is a flexible, low-commitment way to understand Lima’s coastal setting.
visitFlow: Start near Parque del Amor.
Follow the coastal paths toward Larcomar and stop where visibility is clearest.
items.tradeoffs: Mostly easy walking with wind and changing coastal visibility.

items.name: Barranco & Bridge of Sighs
items.summary: Colourful streets, galleries and the little bridge make an atmospheric neighbourhood walk.
items.expect: Street art, cafés and slopes toward the coast.
items.tip: Visit in daylight, then have an early dinner; ask before photographing residents.
items.priceNote: Street walk is free; galleries and food extra.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Colourful streets, galleries and murals make visual culture part of the neighbourhood walk.
The Bridge of Sighs and coastal slopes give the route a distinct small-scale setting.
visitFlow: Walk the central streets in daylight.
Cross the bridge, browse a gallery if open and finish with a planned meal.
items.tradeoffs: Street art, cafés and slopes toward the coast.

items.name: Plaza Mayor & historic centre
items.summary: Colonial plazas and monumental buildings show another side of the capital.
items.expect: Traffic-heavy transfers and crowded streets; many interiors charge separately.
items.tip: Arrange transport both ways and stay on established visitor routes.
items.priceNote: Planning allowance for optional church or museum entry; square itself free.

whyVisit: The main plaza gathers monumental civic and religious architecture.

dayClusters.label: Miraflores archaeology, crafts and coast
dayClusters.note: Check the Huaca tour slot first, browse nearby craft stalls, then walk the coastal paths. Use short rides between inland Miraflores and the cliffs as needed.

dayClusters.label: Historic Lima and Museo Larco
dayClusters.note: Visit the central streets in daylight, then transfer to Pueblo Libre for Museo Larco. These are two districts: allow a substantial taxi/traffic buffer rather than treating them as one walking route.

dayClusters.label: A coastal lunch and Barranco afternoon
dayClusters.note: Have lunch in Miraflores, then transfer to Barranco for galleries and the neighbourhood walk. The spare time is useful for restaurant reservations or weather changes.
